title: GPU Interlock Handoff Canvas — SRE Rapid Triage & Runbook Draft
content:
Purpose:
This is a working canvas to unify on-call observations, early hypotheses, and a first-draft runbook for the class of intermittent multi-epoch GPU node lockups we've been seeing across the west-prod cluster. Goal is to make handoffs predictable: what SRE oncall should try in the first 20/60/180 minutes, what to capture for postmortem signal, and which vendor/infra teams to loop in once we have reproducible captures.

Context / why this is different from previous writeups:
- Symptoms are not a single-failure mode: short ECC bursts, transient NVLink negotiation failures, followed by driver SIGSEGVs in the kernel module and, in several cases, a downstream kernel panic.
- Incidents often self-resolve after node restart but recur on the same hardware over days -> hints at a degradation or timing-sensitive interconnect issue rather than purely random cosmic bitflips.
- We have partial traces: nvlink resets and 'link training failed' logs preceding driver stack dumps, but correlation windows are noisy.

Recent examples seen in the field (summary):
- 2029-08-23 03:12 UTC: ECC-correctable spike on node gpu-45; nvlink negotiation error 2s later; nvidia-driver crashed with oops; kernel panic on next workload start.
- 2029-08-29 19:47 UTC: sustained ECC bursts across two adjacent GPUs in a chassis; both reported id mismatch during nvlink handshake; driver recovered after module reload, but job lost commit.
- 2029-08-31 01:03 UTC: driver SIGSEGV in drm/nvkm stack; dmesg shows 'nvlink timeout waiting for peer' 120ms prior.

Immediate oncall checklist (first 0–20m):
1) Identify affected node and preferred restart window. Do not reboot during heavy jobs if we can migrate: apply low-latency reroute (route away) and enable autoscale fallback.
2) Grab live captures (if node still up):
   - nvidia-smi -q -d ERRORS > /tmp/ecc-snapshot-$(date +%s).txt
   - journalctl -k -u nvidia-driver --since "-30min" > /tmp/driver-journal.txt (adjust unit name to our packaging)
   - dmesg --ctime --follow > /tmp/dmesg-tail.log (pipe to a file for 30s)
   - collect nvlink state: cat /sys/kernel/debug/nvlink/*  (if available) or vendor CLI
   - capture stacktraces: echo t > /proc/sysrq-trigger if driver hangs (only if we can tolerate); collect vmcore if crash completed
3) Snapshot GPU telemetry (prometheus queries):
   - rate(gpu_ecc_correctable_total[5m]) per gpu
   - increase sampling: query node exporter metrics at 5s scrape for the affected node for the next 10–15m (use debug scrape config)
4) Tag the incident pubsub/ops channel with node, tenant, job id, and attach file links.

Deeper triage (20–60m):
- Correlate timelines: ECC bursts -> nvlink negotiation -> driver oops -> kernel panic. Build consolidated timeline with absolute timestamps and event IDs.
- Check adjacency: are failures restricted to GPUs that share an NVSwitch / same PCIe root complex?
- Check BIOS/firmware drift: firmware mismatch history (we've seen cases where one card was updated earlier and started negotiating differently).
- Check for thermal or power anomalies: PSU logs and per-GPU power draw spikes.

Runbook (first stable draft):
Phase A (minimize blast radius):
- Move new traffic off node: mark node DRAINING in scheduler and set low routing weight. (operator: infra-scheduler)
- If driver is still loaded but kernel stack shows hang, attempt safe module unload: modprobe -r nvidia  (only with supervision). If unload fails -> avoid repeated unloads; escalate.
- If job cannot be migrated (stateful), schedule a maintenance window and do graceful host reboot. Preserve /var/crash & /var/log/nvidia* to an attached NFS for analysis.

Phase B (capture & attempt soft remediation):
- Collect full crash artifacts: vmcore, coredumps (systemd-coredump), full journal, /sys/kernel/debug/nvlink snapshots.
- Try driver rollback (if recent driver update): set validated driver kernel module (use curated module from infra-artifacts) and re-run a short synthetic workload to validate (latency-sensitive).
- Toggle nvlink/p2p: use vendor tools to disable nvlink on pair (if hardware supports per-link disable) and test if error recurs. Document exact commands and times.

Phase C (hardware isolation & vendor escalation):
- If recurs within 24h after soft remediation, take node out of pool and run bench of interconnect (vendor stress test + memtester + nvlink loopback tests).
- Collect serial console logs and vendor-level logs; open a vendor SR and attach timelines, NVLink peer IDs, ECC counters, kernel oops, and any firmware versions.

Telemetry queries & dashboard needs (action items):
- Short term queries to add to the incident channel (copyable):
  - SELECT time, gpu_id, ecc_corrected, ecc_uncorrected FROM gpu_errors WHERE time > now() - interval '1 hour' AND node = 'NODE';
  - PromQL: increase(max_over_time(gpu_ecc_correctable_total[15m]), by (instance, gpu)) to spot bursts
- Dashboard: a multi-series timeline with ECC corrected/uncorrected, nvlink negotiation errors, kernel oops count, and driver module reloads aligned to a single timescale.

Hypotheses (back-of-envelope probabilities):
- 40%: NVLink link training degradation due to firmware mismatch or retimer timing drift -> causes negotiation failure sequence that exposes driver race.
- 25%: Driver/kernel-level race condition that only manifests under specific nvlink timing/power conditions (we have a reproducible PR that triggered similar stacktrace in 2028-12).
- 20%: Intermittent PCIe signal integrity / retimer hardware degradation causing transient ECC bursts and consequent link reset.
- 15%: Environmental (PSU instability, PSU fan speed control causing power droops under burst load).

Lab repro plan (if node taken offline):
- Step 1: Replicate NVLink traffic load using vendor stress tool (nvlink-loop or vendor-specific stress binary) for 30–60m while tailing ECC metrics.
- Step 2: Run driver under debug build (with extra ASSERTs/logging) to try to capture exact stack on oom/oops window.
- Step 3: Incrementally enable/disable features: p2p, nvlink flow control, link-training flags exposed in bios/firmware.

Preservation checklist (what to attach to SRE ticket):
- /var/log/messages and journal for +/- 30m around the event
- nvlink sysfs snapshots and any vendor log bundle
- Driver module version and package id (dkms details) + kernel version
- vmcore or kdump output (if panic)
- Workload reproducibility instructions and job id

Open questions (to resolve in postmortem):
- Are the ECC bursts physically causing link retraining, or are they a downstream symptom of an already-failing link?
- Can we add higher-resolution ECC telemetry at the node-agent level without overwhelming Prometheus? (probe: 1–5s temporary)
- Do we have a safe automated fallback to a non-nvlink-only routing when these errors spike above threshold?

Short-term action items (owners):
- Ethan: add high-resolution ECC scrape job for affected pool (temp 5s) and create dashboard panel. (ETA 2029-09-05)
- Rao: draft vendor SR template pre-populated with our typical timeline & artifact list. (ETA 2029-09-06)
- Priya: prepare a driver-rollback playbook with validated rollback bundles in infra-artifacts. (ETA 2029-09-08)
- Sofia: consolidate this canvas into a clean runbook and schedule a 60m playtest with oncall rotation next week. (ETA 2029-09-12)

Notes to self / rough heuristics:
- If ECC corrected spikes > 100 in < 10m on a single GPU, treat as 'urgent' and move traffic off node.
- If nvlink negotiation error appears in dmesg within 5s of ECC spike, capture sysfs immediately — that snapshot is ephemeral.
- Avoid gratuitous cold reboots without collecting vmcore & serial logs. Reboots are fine for restart but hurt postmortem fidelity.

Appendix: useful commands (copy/paste friendly)
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,serial,ecc.mode.ecc,temperature.gpu,clocks.sm --format=csv -q > /tmp/gpu-inventory-$(date +%F-%T).csv
- journalctl -k --since "2029-09-01 00:00:00" | sed -n '1,400p' > /tmp/kernel-journal.txt
- for g in $(nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index --format=csv,noheader); do echo GPU $g; nvidia-smi -i $g --query-gpu=memory.total,memory.free,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory --format=csv; done
- (vendor) nvlink-cli --list-links && nvlink-cli --dump-state > /tmp/nvlink-state.txt

End state/next meeting:
- Convert canvas to final runbook after 1 validation playtest.
- If vendor SRs show hardware-level causes on >= 2 nodes, plan for controlled fleet rollback of affected firmware/drivers and pre-notify customers.

Unresolved: this doc is intentionally conversational. If you pick this up oncall, add your timestamps and small notes inline (e.g., "Sofia: captured sysfs at 2029-09-03T04:12Z") so the eventual postmortem has a live timeline.

-- Sofia A.
(working draft; do not treat as canonical runbook until playtest passes)
